book.rats.name: book.rats.start.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
The rat start gives six rats of the usual ages and sexes. Each carries a random standard coat over an ordinary allele and one inherited strength. Breed them together to mix coats and traits. Two parents with only ordinary coat alleles have a 1 in 32 chance per pup of producing a new standard coat.

After closing the shop, visit Quayside Canning Co-op and open RATS + CARE. Standard coat varieties are sold individually from day 7. Hairless, heavy and cow-spotted milk lines arrive on day 14; rare coats on day 21. Each animal offer renews once per seven-day stock period.

Use the normal animal cage, feed dispenser, marking pen, weighing, feeding, mating and butchering tools. Growth, sex, health, hygiene, disease, pregnancy, overcrowding and mating limits follow the base game. Leave room for growing animals and new litters; a good breeder needs more care, not less.

book.rats.name: book.rats.traits.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
The animal tooltip calls out inherited strengths and weaknesses using its native expressed genes. A trait at I is at least 20% above the species baseline; II is at least 50%. Thrifty eater needs at least 20% or 35% lower hunger demand instead.

Breeder: fertility. Large litters: offspring potential. Meaty: growth and actual body weight. Long-lived: old-age threshold. Hardy: immunity. Sturdy: maximum health. Thrifty eater: hunger demand.

These names describe the genes; they do not stack another buff. Current care, age, disease and native treatment bonuses can change performance. Traits can be inherited from either sex, including litter potential from a male.

book.rats.name: book.rats.selection.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Compare parents, keep useful offspring and breed the next generation. The game chooses one allele from each parent for every native statistic and applies its normal mutation rules. Offspring are not guaranteed copies or guaranteed improvements.

Starter lines offer different strengths: Charcoal/Smoke favour breeding and litter size; Slate/Blue-grey favour meat growth but eat more; Chestnut/Fawn live longer; Russet/Cinnamon favour immunity and health; Olive agouti/Cream eat less but grow a little slower. Cross lines to combine strengths.

The native marking pen can help identify keepers. Physical statistics remain continuous, so two animals with the same trait name can still differ. Negative labels identify genes below baseline.

book.rats.name: book.rats.coats.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Five ordinary coat families have distinct male and female palettes: Charcoal/Smoke, Slate/Blue-grey, Chestnut/Fawn, Russet/Cinnamon, Olive agouti/Cream. These use refined native rat bodies at all five original weight stages, including dead poses. Sex remains the native male/female state.

Each pup receives one coat allele from each parent. Different standard coats express the earlier family in the list while keeping both alleles. A standard coat expresses over normal or rare. Coats do not change fertility or health by themselves.

This is a simple game breeding model. Visible colour does not reveal every carried allele. Keep breeding records.

book.rats.name: book.rats.rare.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Pearl, Champagne and Silver are the three rare coats; each is available in either sex. A rare coat shows only when both inherited alleles match. Rare x normal gives normal-looking carriers. Two carriers of the same rare coat can give about one rare pup in four over many births. Different rare coats do not combine into a free new premium colour.

Extra furry is a separate recessive trait. Both fur alleles must be present for visible tufts. The Russet/Cinnamon starter line carries two; cross it into any coat. Fur does not enlarge the inventory footprint or grant health.

Coat, fur and physical genetics save on the animal. A pregnant female also saves the father's contribution until birth.

book.rats.name: book.rats.market.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: Care and weight still determine the meat yield. Live rats also have a pet value. Standard coats add 15%, rare coats add 100%, and shaggy fur adds 15%. Markings and breeding traits add value when you buy or sell a rat.\n\nRats and fish share 40 breeding traits. Young can take after either parent or develop a new trait. Seven traits on one offspring is a one-in-10,000 birth. Upper-level regulars, Amara Dune and Mina Rose buy pets at the counter.

book.rats.name: book.rats.markings.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Traits also change the rat itself, in every coat and native growth stage.

Meaty: a fuller back and body. Sturdy: a broader shoulder. Extra furry: a rough, tufted outline.

Breeder: a pale flank saddle. Large litters: a pale belly. Long-lived: a pale muzzle. Hardy: a dark back stripe. Thrifty eater: a pale rump. These markings are game breeding-line identifiers, not real-world diagnoses. They can combine on one animal.

The look follows expressed inherited strengths. It does not reveal hidden carrier genes, exact performance, pregnancy or disease. Most I and II markings share a visual family; Meaty II develops a very heavy body after reaching 180 g. Inspect the native stats to compare quality. Colour, texture and markings survive saving and growing without changing cage footprints.

book.rats.name: book.rats.hairless.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Hairlessness is a second recessive form at the coat-texture locus. Two hairless alleles produce bare skin with folds; one hidden allele is carried without showing. Extra-furry x hairless parents produce smooth-looking carriers of both forms. Later generations can express either, according to the inherited pair. Existing smooth and extra-furry lines keep their genes.

Meaty II animals use a very heavy body after reaching 180 g through normal growth. They keep their native weight stages, meat yield and cage rules. Heavy starter stock has stronger growth genes and a bigger appetite, but starts at normal newborn weight. If starvation reduces weight below 180 g, the heavy body stops showing.

Hairless and heavy-line male/female starters arrive on RATS + CARE from day 14, one per weekly stock period. Hairless 90 credits; heavy line 100.

Colours remain inherited independently. On hairless animals they appear as warm skin pigmentation. Heavy builds combine with smooth, shaggy or hairless skin; crossing lines may take several generations. Neither hairlessness nor the heavy appearance adds a separate price or health bonus.

book.rats.name: book.rats.milk.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Cow spots identify an inherited milk line, in any colour, texture or body build. Two milk-line alleles are needed for visible spots. Males pass the line to offspring but do not produce milk. A cross with an ordinary rat gives unspotted carriers; two carriers can produce spotted pups. Quayside stocks both sexes from day 14, 100 credits each, one per week.

Raise a female to native maturity and breed her normally. After a litter, the next seven fed care cycles provide up to 10 mL of collectable surplus per day. This is a game-scale allowance after nursing. Uncollected surplus does not accumulate; starvation or death stops collection. Repeated clicks and reloads do not refill it.

Select the nursing rat, then target an owned bottle, jug or other compatible liquid container. At least 1 mL of space is needed. Only what fits is collected; the rest stays available for that care cycle. Empty bottles remain reusable. Milk contains native water, protein, fat and sugar components and has a creamy colour. Pour it between containers or mix through the ordinary liquid system. Diseased stock can contaminate the liquid; spots do not certify health.

Keep the cage fed, clean and roomy. Milk does not change native litter size, meat yield or sale premiums.

book.rats.name: book.fish.tank.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: These are the original tilapia, gutter tilapia, graft tilapia, eels, electric eels and sturgeon. Individual fish keep their species IDs, tank space, power, water, diets, waste, predation and harvesting rules. Selected juveniles still need raising. Colours do not make a fish immune to poor care.\n\nOpen Quayside's FISH + CARE shelf and click NEXT SPECIES to cycle through all six fish. The shelf stocks each ordinary colour from day 14 and rare colours from day 28, one individual per weekly offer. Selected eel and sturgeon pairs can now breed through the normal tank lifecycle. Male sturgeon are sold on this shelf; the original sturgeon shop stock remains female. Only females produce caviar. Read each species' normal tooltip.

book.rats.name: book.fish.appearance.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: Five standard colour families have distinct male and female palettes: Bronze/Copper, Moss/Olive, Cobalt/Blue-grey, Charcoal/Smoke and Red/Coral. Pearl, Gold and Platinum are three rare colour lines. Eels have Bronze, Olive, Slate, Charcoal and Russet coats, with rare Ivory, Gold and Silver. Sturgeon have Bronze, Olive, Steel-blue, Graphite and Copper, with rare Pearl, Gold and Platinum. The art preserves native fins, plates, scales, outlines and stage sizes.\n\nBody colour, fin colour and markings are three separate inherited pairs. Broad bars, golden bands, blotched pearl, warm-throat, peppered and marbled patterns can combine with red, gold, blue or pale fins. Mixed fin or pattern alleles remain carriers until a matching pair is inherited. Eels instead express lateral ribbons, gold flecks, olive mottling, saddle bands, rare piebald patches or rare ivory marbling. Sturgeon express pale scutes, bronze scutes, silver peppering, copper saddles, rare pearl marbling or rare ivory armour. Default fin genes follow the body's palette. These are simplified game genetics, not a real species' genetic chart.

book.rats.name: book.fish.breeding.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: The native laying, fertilisation and hatch loops remain in control for all six species. Eel clutches contain three fry (5% base laying chance, electric eels 4%); sturgeon clutches contain two (3%). Fertilised eggs hatch on the next tank cycle. Eel fry need three fed growth days; sturgeon fry need four. These are balanced game breeding lines, not a simulation of real eel reproduction. Each unfertilised roe cohort records the laying female's genes. A fed adult male of the same species contributes when native fertilisation happens. Keep a single selected pair together to control parentage; with several eligible males, the father is chosen from them.\n\nAt fertilisation, each offspring receives one allele from each parent at every locus, and its sex is fixed. The whole clutch is saved. Fry visibly show those saved colours and markings, simplified at their small size, and keep them as they grow into individual fish. Roe and fry retain both parents' gene pairs through saves. Siblings can differ. Rare colours need two matching alleles; rare x ordinary produces carriers according to the ordinary colour's dominance. New perk and supplier breeding stock can carry common colours and markings. Eggs supplied already fertilised carry a recorded clutch. Two tank parents with only ordinary colour alleles have a 1 in 32 chance per fry of producing a common colour mutation. Previously recorded clutches keep their genes. No cross-species hybrids or extra free fry are spawned.

book.rats.name: book.fish.traits.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Four inherited gene pairs affect the native aquaculture calculations. Two selected alleles give the full benefit; mixed pairs give intermediate effects.

Meaty: up to 20% faster fed growth progress. Native growth calorie costs remain. Mature, well-grown fish show a fuller body.
Long-lived: up to 30% later native old-age threshold; the original mortality roll remains.
Thrifty: up to 20% less maintenance energy, without reducing growth calorie requirements.
Breeder: up to 40% relative increase to a breedable species' laying chance, capped at 100%. No extra roll, no larger free clutch, and normal fertilisation requirements remain.

Faster growth also advances the native biological-age clock. Combine it with longevity if breeding for longer service. Body weight, fillets, medical grafts, caviar and electric output still use native calculations.

book.rats.name: book.fish.value.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: Live fish have a pet value. Standard colours add 15%, rare colours add 100%, and most patterns add 10%. The two rare eel and sturgeon patterns add 40% or 60%. Breeding traits add value when you buy or sell a fish. Fry carry their traits until they grow into individual fish.\n\nRats and fish share 40 breeding traits. Young can take after either parent or develop a new trait. Seven traits on one offspring is a one-in-10,000 birth. Upper-level regulars, Amara Dune and Mina Rose buy pets at the counter.
